page_hint: Ch 6 §8 (mini-case, 'The Post-Lunch Slowdown'); Ch 8 §3 (Scope note; 'n_hosts' derivation); Ch 5 §8 (mini-case, 'served on 8×H100 with vLLM continuous batching')
quoted_clause: Ch 6 §8: "The architecture is memory- and compute-sane at the 10 rps design point but was never sized for the lunch peak." | Ch 8 §3: "n_hosts = 92,000/19,800 ≈ 4.6 → ~5 hosts" | Ch 8 §8: "at ~10 rps the prefill leg alone demands ~12.9 PFLOP/s, so the fleet spans several nodes — Ch 24's prefill screen: 1.63 nodes at 100% MFU, ~5 at 35% MFU"
observed: Ch 6's mini-case asserts the canonical design point is compute-sane on one 8×H100 host. The book's own compute screen (Ch 8 §3) says the opposite: at 10 rps the prefill demand is 92,000 tokens/s (12.9 PFLOP/s) against a per-host sustained prefill rate of ~19,800 tokens/s (2.7692 PFLOP/s at 35% MFU), i.e. ~4.66× oversubscribed, requiring ~5 hosts. Ch 8 §8 states the same ('the fleet spans several nodes ... ~5 at 35% MFU'). Ch 8's Scope note disclaims only the 40 rps peak ('It is not a claim that one host absorbs the 40 rps peak arrival rate'), leaving the 10 rps average implication unstated, and Ch 5's mini-case presents a single 8×H100 host as the architecture for the 10 rps workload.
correction: In Ch 6 §8, replace the design-point claim with the compute screen: 'The architecture is memory-sane at the 10 rps design point but compute-oversubscribed on a single host: 12.9 PFLOP/s of prefill demand against ~2.77 PFLOP/s of sustained per-host capacity (~4.7×), so the canonical fleet is ~5 hosts at 35% MFU (Ch 8 §3).' Extend Ch 8 §3's Scope note to disclaim the 10 rps average as well as the 40 rps peak, and add a one-line qualifier in Ch 5 §8's mini-case that the 8×H100 host is the per-request/per-host container, not the whole fleet.
acceptance_test: A reader who reads Ch 5 §8, Ch 6 §8 and Ch 8 §3 in sequence can state, without contradiction, how many 8×H100 hosts the canonical 10 rps workload needs and why; no sentence in Ch 5/6/8 asserts that one host is compute-sane at 10 rps.
verdict_evidence: ch6:131 'memory- and compute-sane at the 10 rps design point'; ch8:164 gives 92,000/19,800=4.6 to ~5 hosts at 10 rps; ch8:63 scope note disclaims only 40 rps peak; ch5:196 serves 10 rps on one host.
fix_instruction: ch6:131 to 'memory-sane but compute-oversubscribed at 10 rps (~4.7x, ~5 hosts, ch08:164)'; extend ch08:63 scope note to 10 rps; qualify ch05:196.

page_hint: Ch 5 §3, Table 5-2 (row 'Total tokens per dollar'); Ch 5 §3(b) 'tokens/s per dollar with prefill included'
quoted_clause: Table 5-2: "| Total tokens per dollar (prefill + decode, stated concurrency) | ~285,000 tokens per dollar at 300 output tokens/request | 50 × (1 + 9,200/300) ≈ 1,583 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20 [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] |"
observed: The row label says 'stated concurrency', but the derivation contains no concurrency: 50 tok/s is the single-stream decode rate and 9,200/300 is a per-request token ratio, so the figure describes one stream with prefill overlapped (the §3(b) 'continuous batching' case). The row immediately above it is explicitly labelled 'single-stream decode', so the table juxtaposes a single-stream output-token metric with a batched total-token metric without saying so. The prose in §3(b) supplies the missing scope ('the 9,000 tokens-per-dollar figure should be read as a floor set by the single-stream assumption'), but the table — the artifact a reader copies from — loses it.
correction: Relabel the row: 'Total tokens per dollar (single-stream decode + overlapped prefill; not the 10 rps fleet point) | ~285,000 tokens per dollar at 300 output tokens/request' and add a second row for the strictly serial single-stream floor (~242,000 tokens/$) so the two operating points are visible in the table rather than only in prose.
acceptance_test: Every row of Table 5-2 states its operating point (single-stream / overlapped / batched) and its concurrency basis; no reader can take 285,000 tokens/$ as the canonical 10 rps fleet figure.
verdict_evidence: ch5:80 row 'stated concurrency' but 50x(1+9,200/300)=1,583 tok/s is one stream with overlapped prefill; no concurrency number; serial floor 242,000 and 10 rps 95,000 neither figure.
fix_instruction: Relabel ch05:80 'single-stream decode + overlapped prefill; not the 10 rps fleet point' and add the ~242,000 tok/$ serial row from ch05:103.

page_hint: Ch 5 §3(a), Table 5-1 footnote; §3(a) 'The decision hinges on…'; §3(a) Takeaway; §8 mini-case bullet 1
quoted_clause: Footnote: "the proxy ratio (4.8×) is a lower bound on the true body-only compute ratio (≈7.7×), not an upper bound." | Decision text: "justify the ~4.8×FLOP cost (14.08 vs 2.94 GFLOP per 64-token query, Table 5-1)" | Takeaway: "the ~4.8× FLOP cost is paid"
observed: The chapter establishes that the 2×params×L proxy understates the true cross-model compute ratio (4.8× total-params vs ≈7.7× body-only), then uses the understated 4.8× figure as the decision threshold in three places (the decision paragraph, the Takeaway, and the mini-case). The bar the reader is told to apply is therefore the one the chapter has just shown to be the wrong one for a cross-model comparison.
correction: Use one stated bar everywhere: 'the cross-model compute ratio is ≈4.8× on total parameters and ≈7.7× on body parameters (the proxy understates it); the quality gain must clear the body-parameter ratio, ≈7.7×, to justify the larger encoder.' Alternatively, state explicitly that the decision is taken on the Table 5-1 proxy rows and that the true ratio is higher, so the bar is conservative in the wrong direction and must be re-derived before use.
acceptance_test: Every occurrence of the cross-model FLOP-cost ratio in Ch 5 states which parameter basis it uses, and no occurrence uses 4.8× as the decision threshold after the chapter has established 7.7× as the true body-only ratio.
verdict_evidence: ch5:57 calls 4.8x lower bound on true ~7.7x body-only ratio; ch5:67 twice sets bar at '~4.8x FLOP cost (14.08 vs 2.94 GFLOP)'; 110/23=4.78; body 86.1/11.0=7.8.
fix_instruction: At ch05:67 state the bar as ~7.7x body-only (4.8x on total params) and note the 14.08/2.94 GFLOP rows understate the ratio.

verdict_evidence: ch5:159 verbatim carries editorial aside inside reader-facing Common Mistakes bullet; no other section states the convention.

observed: The two arrows from 'Five selection surfaces' are both labeled 'split', which asserts that the five surfaces are partitioned between the retrieval leg and the generation leg. That is not what the caption describes: the five surfaces (quality, latency, KV cache, cost per token, retrieve-vs-generate) are the criteria applied to model selection, and each leg is evaluated against all of them - latency and cost-per-token matter for the embedding model as much as for the generator. As drawn, the figure teaches a partitioning model that the caption's own framing ('the five surfaces are the model-selection dimensions') contradicts, and a reader could conclude that, for example, KV cache is only a generation-leg concern.
acceptance_test: Relabel the two arrows so they do not assert partition (e.g. 'applies to', 'evaluated for'), or draw the five surfaces feeding both legs with a shared bracket. The figure must not imply that any surface applies to only one leg.
verdict_evidence: Both arrows out of 'Five selection surfaces' labelled 'split' (book p114; fig_ch5_rag.py:97) while caption (ch05:200) calls the five items model-selection dimensions distinct from evaluation gates — nothing supports partitioning.
fix_instruction: Relabel both arrows 'applies to' (or bracket the five surfaces across both legs) so no surface reads as belonging to a single leg.
